predictions.claim: LLMs will be superseded by systems that learn directly from experience rather than from human-generated text, repeating the historical pattern of the Bitter Lesson.
predictions.speaker: Richard Sutton
predictions.notes: Sutton frames this as inevitable but doesn't give a tight date — uses decade-scale framing.

predictions.claim: Succession from humans to digital or AI-augmented intelligences is inevitable, given that no global governance exists, intelligence will be understood, capabilities will exceed human level, and intelligent entities accrue power.
predictions.speaker: Richard Sutton
predictions.notes: Framed as structurally inevitable rather than dated.

predictions.claim: Cybersecurity between digital minds — preventing hidden goals or 'viruses' from corrupting an AI that incorporates outside knowledge — will become a major concern in the age of digital spawning.
predictions.speaker: Richard Sutton
predictions.notes: Novel reframing of AI safety as inter-agent cybersecurity.

predictions.claim: Current deep learning has no algorithmic mechanism producing good generalization or transfer; without a new technique, scaled LLMs will continue to rely on researcher hand-tuning rather than emergent generalization.
predictions.speaker: Richard Sutton
